releases.body:
- **bugfix**: serialization now fails fast when a covariance function (or a predictor) belongs to a class that could not be resolved again on loading. Mellon stores classes by name and recovers them with `getattr(import_module(module_name), classname)`, so a class that is not bound at the top level of its module — most commonly one defined inside a factory function — produced a file that `Covariance.from_dict` / `Predictor.from_json` could not load. Previously `to_json()` wrote that file without complaint and the `AttributeError` surfaced only at load time, potentially long after the fit it was meant to preserve. `to_json()` / `to_dict()` now raise a `TypeError` naming the offending qualified name and asking for a module-level definition. Module-level covariance functions, including user-defined ones, are unaffected and still round-trip exactly; existing serialized files still load. `Predictor.copy()` is deliberately not affected, as it never resolves the predictor class by name.
 - the guard above lives in `Covariance.__getstate__`, which is also Python's `copy`/`pickle` hook, so `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle.dumps()` of such a covariance function now raise the same `TypeError`. Previously `deepcopy` succeeded, since it carries the class by reference instead of resolving it by name; `pickle` failed on its own. Only classes that were already unserializable are affected. For the same reason `Predictor.copy()` of a predictor with such a covariance function now raises `TypeError` up front instead of the previous `AttributeError` from the load path — it did not work before either.
 - composite covariance functions (`+`, `*`, `**`) now record the full module of their class instead of only the top-level package, so a user-defined `CovariancePair` subclass living in a subpackage can be resolved on loading. Files written by earlier versions continue to load unchanged.
 - `compute_d_factal` is renamed to **`compute_d_fractal`**, correcting the spelling of "fractal". The new name is the canonical one and is what `d_method="fractal"` now calls internally. **`compute_d_factal` continues to work**: it is retained as an alias that forwards to `compute_d_fractal`, is still exported from `mellon.parameters`, and remains listed in `__all__`, so existing code needs no change. **No deprecation warning is emitted** — the old name is used widely enough downstream that a warning on by default would be noise rather than signal. Callers writing new code should prefer `compute_d_fractal`.
 - **removed**: the `mellon-test` console script. It was declared as `mellon-test = "pytest:main"` while `pytest` is only a `dev` extra, so on a normal install it failed immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest'`. It could not have worked even with `pytest` present: the installed distribution contains only the `mellon` package, never the test suite, and the script invoked `pytest.main()` with no arguments — so it would have collected from whatever directory it happened to be run in. Run the tests from a source checkout with `pytest` instead. **This removes a published command**, so any script invoking `mellon-test` will now get "command not found" rather than the `ModuleNotFoundError` it got before.
 - **bugfix**: declare `packaging` as a runtime dependency. `mellon.base_predictor` has imported `packaging.version` at module scope since v1.5.0, but `packaging` was never listed in the project dependencies, so installing Mellon into an environment that provided only its declared requirements failed at `import mellon` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'packaging'`. Environments that happened to supply `packaging` transitively — including any install of the `dev` or `docs` extras — were unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed. If you have ever hit `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'packaging'` on a fresh install of Mellon, this is the fix.
 - the GP leverage diagonal `diag(B M^-1 B^T)` is now computed with a Cholesky solve instead of an explicit `jnp.linalg.inv(M)`. `M = sigma^2 K_uu + B^T B` (plus jitter) is symmetric positive definite by construction, so the inverse was never needed. All five sites are converted: `_LandmarksConditional._compute_obs_variance` and `._leverage` (scalar and per-feature sigma) and `_LandmarksConditionalCholesky._leverage`. Results are unchanged to within rounding (worst relative difference 1.8e-7 across 30 public-API comparisons; 1.9e-4 on a real 5,000-landmark problem with cond(M) = 2.5e13, where both forms agree with a QR reference to about 1e-4 and neither is uniformly the more accurate).
 - this also removes a segfault. `jnp.linalg.inv` lowers to LU (`getrf`), which dispatches to OpenBLAS's threaded `dgetrf_parallel`; at 5,000 landmarks that routine overflows the stack of the thread JAX calls it on and the process dies with SIGSEGV. Measured on OpenBLAS 0.3.30: 12/12 crashes end-to-end at `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=16` against 0/12 at 1 thread, and 6/12 against 0/12 for the unpatched and patched code run back to back (not concurrently). Affects any caller using landmarks with `obs_variance=True` or `Predictor.leverage()`. The Cholesky path uses `potrf` and is unaffected. `export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` remains a valid workaround on older versions.
 - note: with `jitter=0`, or in float32, the Cholesky form returns NaN for matrices where the old `inv` returned finite values. In every such case checked the old values were numerically meaningless (errors above 25%, leverages outside [0, 1]), so this surfaces a failure that was previously silent. The default `jitter=1e-6` in float64 — what every estimator uses — is unaffected.
